answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy starts with a cost that cannot be faked cheaply. One concrete mechanism: each new agent stakes a small bond, and payouts unlock only after independent peers attest its work across several epochs. An attacker building a dune of fresh identities finds every copy must fund its own bond, and each bond idles until real graded work clears it, so a wide ridge of fake accounts costs capital plus time. Reputation is then tinted with a durable pigment: scores follow attested history, not self-declared names, so clones inherit nothing. Cheap swarm, expensive proof.
